rationale: Whole-tree lowering deliberately does not carry `transform`, because the box a node is placed by is already the transformed rectangle. That is true of the box and false of everything inside it: Chrome scales the glyphs along with the box, so a pre-scaled box filled with the untransformed `font-size` drew every run 1/scale too wide. On forge, 25 of 39 text runs sit under one `transform: matrix(0.9,0,0,0.9,0,0)` wrapper and the headline 'What do you want to build?' rendered 11.10% long, ending at x=1904 against Chrome's x=1800. Lowering now folds the accumulated ancestor scale into font-size, letter-spacing and line-height. Ancestor chains multiply rather than taking the nearest wrapper's factor. A chain that does not reduce to one positive uniform scale — two axes, a flip, a rotation, a matrix3d — is REFUSED and recorded per node as `type_scale_refused` plus a `native_nodes_type_scale_refused` count, because type carries a single scalar and a plausible wrong number is harder to find later than a recorded refusal. Measured: the headline goes to +0.00% and ends at x=1800, Chrome's own pixel; forge's rendered ink width across every measurable run moves from median +7.04% p95 +11.63% to median +0.00% p95 +1.16%, and for the 16 runs under the wrapper from +10.85% to +0.00%; area-weighted failing 0.1691 to 0.1635 and the text feature 0.4384 to 0.3634 at unchanged 1.0000 coverage. Designs with no transform are untouched, asserted by byte equality rather than by argument: delay and spectr render 0 changed pixels and hold at 0.0944 and 0.1245. A new capture fixture renders one string twice at an identical computed style where the only difference is a scale(0.5) wrapper — Chrome reports 143.188px and 286.375px — so a lowering that ignored the transform cannot pass by arithmetic over the computed style alone. Pulp-only: the defect and the fix both originate here.
